primitives.name: Home Court Advantage Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: State University Perceived Schedule Effects • Fitted SLR of home MOV on Vegas Line (V) in the NBA: \ MOV = 0.01 + .95V • Fatigue effects on spread highly significant.
primitives.assumptions: Linear relationship between Vegas line and margin of victory; homoscedastic error structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When V approaches zero or exceeds typical spread ranges, model may underpredict MOV.

primitives.verbatim_quote: (See map courtesy of reddit user: cs irl) • After adjustment for scheduling discrepancy using factorial effects in linear/generalized linear models, much of the home ice advantage in the NHL vanishes.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that scheduling effects—particularly fatigue and rest—introduce systematic bias into game outcomes. In the NBA, a fitted simple linear regression shows that MOV (margin of victory) scales with the Vegas line (V), indicating that betting markets implicitly account for home advantage but also reflect underlying fatigue. The r² = 0.82 suggests strong explanatory power of the model, while MSE = 2.9 indicates acceptable residual error. Adjusting for schedule discrepancies using factorial effects removes much of the home ice advantage in the NHL, implying that perceived advantages are often artifacts of scheduling rather than true competitive strength. This reveals a dual nature of performance: one governed by inherent team quality and another by temporal and logistical constraints. The implications for GSI involve correcting for these biases in betting models, while GSE must incorporate them into dynamic state transitions to predict optimal strategies. Failure modes include ignoring non-linear fatigue curves or assuming uniform rest across teams.
